NutriFresh Foods - Q2 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Foods Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a landline or click the Q&A button in the webcast if online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Foods' Q2 FY2024 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q2 FY2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: overall company performance highlights, e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, organic revenue growth overall and by region, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year, gross margin analysis drivers and trends, and impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions.

First, regarding overall company performance highlights: I'm thrilled to walk you through our Q2 results, which underscore the resilience and strategic execution of our diversified portfolio in this dynamic Food & Beverage landscape. We delivered another quarter of solid outcomes, navigating persistent inflationary pressures, shifting consumer behaviors, and supply chain headwinds while capitalizing on our premiumization strategy and innovation pipeline.

Starting with the top line: Q2 net revenues reached $1.25 billion, up 6.2% year-over-year, or 7% on an organic basis excluding acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange impacts. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of organic growth, outpacing the broader F&B category, which per NielsenIQ data grew just 2.1% in measured channels. Breaking it down, pricing actions contributed 3.9 percentage points to growth—strategically implemented across 85% of our SKU portfolio to offset raw material inflation in commodities like cocoa, sugar, and dairy, which peaked at +28% YoY earlier this year but have moderated to +12% in Q2. Volume/mix added a healthy 0.9 points, driven by strong velocity in our health & wellness segment and market share gains in snacks.

Adjusted EPS came in at $1.12, a robust 8.7% increase from $1.03 last year, beating our guidance midpoint and reflecting disciplined cost management. Reported EPS was $1.05, with the variance primarily from one-time restructuring charges related to our North American plant rationalization. Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 38.4%, our strongest in five quarters, fueled by supply chain efficiencies and a favorable mix shift toward higher-margin plant-based and RTD beverages. Operating margin held steady at 14.2%, as SG&A investments in digital commerce and trade promotion offset some gains.

Segment-wise, our Snacks & Confectionery division, which represents 42% of revenues, surged 7.5% organically to $525 million. Market share in the U.S. salty snacks category climbed to 14.2% per IRI, up 60 basis points, propelled by our Velocity Crunch line of air-popped veggie chips, which posted 22% dollar growth and expanded distribution to 92% ACV in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club. Premium chocolate bars benefited from cocoa hedging programs we locked in at $4,200 per ton back in Q1, shielding us from the +45% spot price spike.

Beverages, 35% of the portfolio, grew 5.1% organically to $437 million. Non-alcoholic RTD segment was the star, up 12% with our NutriSpark functional waters—infused with electrolytes and adaptogens—gaining traction amid the wellness boom. Carbonated soft drinks faced headwinds from consumer trading down to private label, but our pricing discipline and zero-sugar variants limited volume decline to -1.2%, versus category -3.5%. In dairy alternatives, oat milk volumes rose 18%, capturing share from incumbents as lactose intolerance claims drive +9% category growth.

Our Health & Wellness platform, now 18% of revenues at $225 million, accelerated 9.3% organically—our fastest-growing unit. Plant-based proteins, including our NutriHarvest patties reformulated with pea-rice blends for better texture and 20% less sodium, achieved 25% growth and broke into 75% ACV at Whole Foods and Kroger. This aligns with the seismic shift in F&B: Nielsen reports plant-based sales up 15% YoY, even as overall protein category softens.

International performance was a bright spot, contributing 28% of revenues. EMEA delivered 8.2% organic growth to $186 million, led by premium yogurt expansions in the UK and Germany, where we gained 1.2 share points against competitors amid 'clean label' demand. APAC surged 11.4% to $162 million, with RTD teas and functional snacks thriving in China and India—our WeChat Mini Program e-commerce sales jumped 45%, tapping into the $150B digital F&B market projected by Statista. Latin America grew 4.1% despite FX volatility, bolstered by cost-sharing JVs with local bottlers.

Regionally in North America, our core market at 72% of revenues, we posted 3.9% organic growth to $900 million. While at-home consumption remains pressured by +4% grocery inflation per USDA data, our away-from-home channels—QSR and convenience—grew 7%, with snack pairings in quick-service restaurants and convenience stores driving velocity. Market share across CPG channels held at 11.8%, per Circana, insulating us from private label encroachment.

Operationally, we've leaned into technical initiatives to sustain momentum. Our Enterprise Resource Planning upgrade to SAP S/4HANA, now live across 80% of plants, yielded $45 million in procurement savings through AI-driven demand forecasting, reducing inventory by 15% and waste by 22%—critical as food waste regulations tighten. Sustainability remains core: Scope 1 & 2 emissions down 18% YoY via regenerative agriculture with 250,000 acres of supplier farmland, positioning us ahead of peers. On innovation, we launched 14 SKUs this quarter, with 70% in premium health formats, and our R&D spend rose to 2.8% of revenues.

Strategically, we're executing our 'Fresh Forward' framework: portfolio right-sizing by divesting 15 low-margin legacy SKUs, which unlocked $120 million in proceeds for bolt-on M&A. Consumer insights from our 50,000-panelist community show 68% prioritizing 'functional benefits'—hence our push into gut-health probiotics and low-GI snacks. Amid economic uncertainty, we're balancing value plays like multi-packs with premium tiers, where 55% of sales now command 20%+ price premiums.

Balance sheet remains fortress-like: $1.2 billion in cash, net debt to EBITDA at 2.1x, and operating cash flow of $450 million in Q2, up 14%. We repurchased $150 million in shares and raised our dividend 5% to $0.42 per share.

Second, concerning e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: One of our most exciting growth drivers this quarter has been our e-commerce sales performance and its expanding contribution to total revenue. The Food & Beverage sector has seen a seismic shift since the pandemic, with e-commerce penetration accelerating from single digits pre-2020 to now averaging 12-15% across public peers. For NutriFresh Foods, we're leading the pack.

Total net revenue came in at $1.25 billion, up 6% year-over-year on a reported basis and 7% on an organic constant-currency basis, driven by volume gains in core categories—healthy snacks, functional beverages, and ready-to-eat meals—and modest pricing actions to offset input cost inflation. Within that, e-commerce sales reached $210 million, representing a robust 28% year-over-year growth. That's our 12th straight quarter of double-digit e-com expansion. Importantly, e-commerce now accounts for 16.8% of total revenue, up from 13.2% a year ago and more than double the 7.5% it contributed back in FY2021. This outperforms the broader F&B industry benchmark of around 10-12% penetration, as reported by NielsenIQ, and puts us ahead of peers like Campbell Soup at about 14%, or PepsiCo's direct channels near 11%.

Breaking it down by channel, our direct-to-consumer platform—powered by our NutriFresh Direct app and website—delivered $85 million, up 35% YoY, fueled by recurring subscription revenue from our Protein Boost shakes and Snack Box bundles, which now make up 42% of DTC sales. Average order value here climbed 12% to $68, thanks to personalized upsell algorithms recommending complementary items like our new Zero-Sugar Energy Waters alongside high-protein bars. Customer acquisition costs held steady at $18 per new subscriber, while lifetime value improved to $420, giving us a healthy 23x LTV-to-CAC ratio.

On the marketplace side, third-party platforms contributed $125 million, up 24% YoY. Amazon remains our powerhouse, accounting for 55% of marketplace GMV via Prime Now and Amazon Fresh integrations. Our Velocity Snacks line saw a 40% surge there, capturing share in the on-the-go segment amid rising demand for low-carb, plant-based options. Partnerships with Instacart and DoorDash drove 30% growth in quick-commerce, particularly for our ReadyMeals portfolio, where same-day delivery penetration hit 22% in urban markets. Basket sizes on these platforms averaged 2.8 SKUs per order, up from 2.4 last year, as shoppers consolidate trips amid inflationary pressures.

Regionally, North America, which represents 72% of our e-com revenue, sales grew 32% YoY to $151 million, or 19% of regional total revenue. This was propelled by our West Coast fulfillment center expansion in Reno, Nevada, which cut delivery times to under 2 hours for 65% of orders and boosted conversion rates by 18% through real-time inventory syncing. We're seeing strong traction in the Sun Belt states, where functional beverages like our Electrolyte Hydrators are outperforming, up 45% on Walmart+.

Europe delivered 22% growth to $38 million, now 12% of regional revenue, despite a softer macro backdrop. Our UK business via Ocado and Tesco online grew 29%, benefiting from post-Brexit supply chain optimizations. In Germany and France, GDPR-compliant personalization engines—leveraging first-party data from our loyalty program—lifted repeat purchase rates to 68%. For perishables like our Fresh Yogurt Parfaits with a 5-day shelf life, we've invested in micro-fulfillment hubs in Berlin and Paris to maintain 98% on-time delivery.

Asia-Pacific is our fastest-growing region at 42% YoY to $21 million, though it's still just 9% of regional revenue given our nascent footprint. China via Tmall and JD.com was the star, with 55% growth on our imported Superfruit Juices, tapping into the premiumization trend where consumers are trading up 15-20% YoY per Kantar data. In India, BigBasket and Blinkit partnerships drove 60% gains in urban metros for our Masala Nut mixes, though rural logistics remain a hurdle—we're piloting drone deliveries with local startups to address last-mile costs, which currently run 25% higher than in mature markets.

Technically, our AI-powered recommendation engine, built on Google Cloud's Vertex AI, analyzes over 50 behavioral signals—from browse time to past AOV—to drive a 22% uplift in cross-sell rates. We've rolled this out to 80% of our DTC traffic. Omnichannel sync via Shopify Plus and our ERP system ensures seamless inventory visibility, reducing stockouts by 35% and enabling buy online, pick up in-store for 15% of e-com orders. We're experimenting with AR virtual try-ons for beverage mixology—scan a QR on our app to \"pour\" a mocktail—which has boosted engagement 40% among Gen Z shoppers. On the backend, blockchain tracing for our organic lines enhances trust, aligning with consumer demands per the FMI's 2024 report, where 62% of online F&B buyers prioritize traceability.

Strategically, e-commerce isn't just a revenue lever—it's a margin expander and innovation engine. Gross margins on DTC sales hit 48%, versus 38% in traditional grocery, thanks to eliminated slotting fees and trade spend. This added 120 basis points to our overall blended gross margin in Q2. Moreover, e-com data is gold for R&D: insights from basket analysis revealed a 30% affinity between our Keto Bars and CBD-infused waters, spawning a new co-branded bundle launching Q4. We're also using it to refine pricing dynamically—testing 5-10% premiums on high-demand items without velocity loss.

Looking ahead, we're guiding e-commerce to $950 million for FY2024, implying 26% growth and 17.5% of total revenue, with ambitions to hit 22% by FY2026 through further capex in automation—$150 million allocated, including two new automated micro-fuls in Southeast Asia. Risks include channel conflict with retailers like Kroger and Whole Foods, which we're mitigating via exclusive online SKUs, and softening consumer sentiment; however, our value tiers and loyalty perks position us resiliently.

Third, in terms of progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: As we continue to execute on our long-term growth strategy, I'm pleased to provide an update on our sustainability initiatives, which remain a cornerstone of our value creation. In our industry, where resource intensity meets rising consumer expectations and regulatory pressures, sustainability isn't just about compliance—it's a competitive differentiator driving margin expansion, brand loyalty, and innovation pipelines. We've made significant strides across our 2023 Sustainability Roadmap, advancing toward our 2030 Science-Based Targets.

First, on sustainable sourcing, which accounts for over 70% of our Scope 3 emissions. We've now achieved 92% responsibly sourced key commodities globally, up from 85% last year. This includes 100% Rainforest Alliance-certified cocoa for our Heritage Chocolate line—and 95% sustainably sourced coffee for our NutriBrew pods, verified through the 4C Association and now expanding into regenerative programs. In palm oil, we're at 98% RSPO-certified segregated supply, avoiding deforestation-linked suppliers entirely. Regionally, APAC has been our star performer at 96% compliance, driven by our joint ventures in Indonesia, while LATAM hit 90% amid supply chain disruptions from last year's El Niño impacts on sugarcane yields. These efforts have unlocked $45 million in cost savings through premium pricing on certified products, with sustainable SKUs growing 18% YoY in sales velocity.

Water stewardship is another pillar, critical for our beverage segment, which represents 40% of revenues. We've reduced absolute water withdrawal by 22% since 2020, hitting 15.5 billion liters in 2023—below our interim 18 billion liter target—through precision irrigation tech like drip systems and AI-driven sensors deployed across 65% of our 120 global bottling plants. In water-stressed regions like California's Central Valley and India's Maharashtra, we've achieved 35% reductions via closed-loop recycling, partnering with the Alliance for Water Stewardship. This mitigates risks from droughts and has improved our Water Risk Index score to 'low' from 'medium' per WWF assessments.

On packaging, we're ahead of schedule toward 100% recyclable, compostable, or reusable by 2025. Recycled content now averages 28% across our portfolio—up from 19%—with rPET at 50% in North American soda bottles and 40% in European dairy packs. We've eliminated 15,000 metric tons of virgin plastic annually through lightweighting, and launched our 'FreshLoop' reusable bottle program in 12 urban markets, capturing 2.5 million returns YTD and reducing single-use packaging by 8%. In Europe, where the PPWR directive looms, this positions us favorably, with 75% of packs compliant already.

Emissions reduction ties directly to our net-zero by 2040 ambition. Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions are down 28% from 2019 baselines, at 1.2 million tCO2e, fueled by 85% renewable energy procurement—think PPAs with solar farms in Texas and wind in Brazil—and electrifying 40% of our fleet with EV partnerships for short-haul dairy distribution. Scope 3 progress is advancing: we've cut it 12% through supplier engagement, with 80% of Tier 1 vendors now on SBTi trajectories. Regenerative agriculture pilots on 250,000 hectares—focusing on soil carbon sequestration in wheat fields for our GrainWave snacks—have boosted yields 15% while drawing down 50,000 tCO2e.

Waste-wise, we've diverted 96% of operational waste from landfills, processing 1.1 million tons via anaerobic digestion for biogas that powers 20% of our EU plants. Food waste in supply chains is down 14% to 2.5% of production, thanks to AI forecasting tools.

Strategically, these initiatives are fueling top-line growth: our 'NutriGreen' portfolio—sustainable variants across beverages, snacks, and plant-based dairy—now 25% of revenues, up 300 bps YoY, with 22% premium pricing power amid 65% consumer willingness-to-pay premiums per Nielsen data. We've hedged commodity volatility through long-term offtake agreements with regen farmers, stabilizing COGS at 2.5% inflation versus industry 5%. Partnerships like our agroforestry initiatives not only secure supplies but enhance our ESG ratings—we're now in the top quintile of the FTSE4Good Index.

Looking ahead, we'll invest $300 million over the next three years in circular economy R&D, targeting bio-based proteins, and blockchain traceability for 100% ingredient transparency by 2026. Risks remain—particularly Scope 3 supplier alignment and geopolitical sourcing shifts—but our diversified footprint and $500 million sustainability-linked bond issuance provide resilience. Sustainability at NutriFresh is delivering tangible ROI: $120 million in savings, 5 ppt EBITDA margin uplift potential, and a moat in a market where 78% of Gen Z shoppers prioritize eco-credentials per Kantar. We're on track, accountable via annual third-party audits.

Fourth, looking at impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: As we examine our financials, a key headwind this quarter has been the impact of foreign exchange rates on our reported revenue. As a global leader with powerhouse brands like Quench Energy Drinks, PureHarvest Juices, and Velocity Nuts, we derive approximately 48% of our net revenue from international markets—spanning premium ready-to-drink beverages in Europe, functional snacks in Asia-Pacific, and value-added dairy alternatives in Latin America. This exposure creates translational FX volatility when converting local-currency sales back to the US dollar, even as it drives our 7% organic growth on a constant currency basis.

For Q2, our reported net revenue was $1.25 billion, up 6% year-over-year. However, on a constant currency basis, revenue grew a robust 7%, aligning with our mid-single-digit growth algorithm. The FX drag stemmed from a 12% strengthening of the USD against key trading partner currencies over the past 12 months, per the Bloomberg Global FX Index for food markets.

Regionally, Europe (25% of total revenue): The euro depreciated 9% year-to-date against the USD, hammering our €1.2 billion in local sales of Quench low-sugar energy drinks and PureHarvest organic juices. This translated to a $92 million FX hit, or 7% of regional revenue. Premium pricing in markets like Germany and the UK held volumes flat, but constant currency gains from e-commerce acceleration via Amazon EU and Ocado partnerships were masked.

Asia-Pacific (12% of revenue): The Japanese yen weakened 11%, contributing a $28 million drag on our snack portfolio, including Velocity's high-protein almond bars popular in convenience stores. The Australian dollar held steady, supporting 10% constant currency growth in RTD coffee. Overall, APAC delivered a net $35 million FX headwind.

Latin America (8% of revenue): Volatility with the Brazilian real down 15% and Mexican peso off 8%, leading to a $42 million impact. Brazil saw resilient demand for value-pack juices, with 12% constant currency growth fueled by localized production. Other international added a $9 million tailwind from INR and ZAR appreciation.

Over the trailing 12 months, FX has shaved 450 basis points off our top-line growth, mirroring industry dynamics—PepsiCo cited a similar drag, while Mondelez reported 400 bps pressure.

On mitigation, our treasury team executed 70% coverage of forecasted exposures using zero-cost collars on forwards and FX options, locking in rates at an average of 1.08 USD/EUR and 5.45 BRL/USD. This shielded $120 million of the hit, delivering 72% hedge effectiveness. Transactionally, 85% of our APAC procurement is now in local currencies, creating natural hedges against input costs for cocoa and nuts.

Looking forward, we expect a $200-250 million FX headwind for full-year 2024, assuming consensus USD strength persists. Strategically, we're pursuing pricing discipline with 2-4% list price increases in Europe and LatAm, preserving our 42% gross margins; supply chain localization with new aseptic bottling lines in Mexico opening Q1 2025; and portfolio mix shift boosting USD-denominated North American sales to 55% of total by FY2026 via innovation in functional beverages like our upcoming Quench Collagen line targeting the $15B US wellness market. While FX is non-operating noise, our constant currency momentum underscores our brands' health.

Fifth, reviewing organic revenue growth overall and by region: Organic revenue growth excludes the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and currency fluctuations. We delivered 5.4% organic revenue growth overall, accelerating from 4.1% in Q1 and marking our strongest quarterly performance in the past 18 months. This outperformance versus peers reflects the resilience of our core brands amid persistent inflation in commodities like sugar, cocoa, and aluminum, and softening consumer demand in value segments.

Organic growth was driven by 2.1% from volume, 2.6% from pricing actions, and 0.7% from favorable product mix. Volume gains were underpinned by our high-margin premium and functional beverage portfolio, including our relaunched NutriSpark energy drinks with adaptogens, which saw 15% household penetration growth per Nielsen data. Pricing averaged 5-7% realized increases across regions, offsetting 12% YoY input cost inflation while maintaining everyday low pricing on hero SKUs like our Fresca Fizz carbonated waters. Mix shift came from premiumization—functional beverages and plant-based snacks now 28% of total revenue, up from 22% a year ago—helping capture share in the $150B+ global health & wellness subsector.

Regionally, North America (55% of total revenue): Robust 7.2% organic growth, fueled by 3.8% volume expansion and 3.4% pricing. This beat our internal plan by 150bps, driven by market share gains in convenient nutrition—our NutriBar protein snacks grew 22% YoY, outpacing category leaders amid the post-pandemic snacking boom. E-commerce accelerated to 18% of NA sales, bolstered by our Amazon Velocity partnership and DTC site enhancements. Our Clean Label Accelerator program reformulated 40% of our beverage portfolio to under 5g sugar per serving, driving 12% trial uplift per IRI data. Challenges in mass-market sodas were mitigated by pivot to RTD coffees, up 19%.

EMEA (25% of revenue): Growth moderated to 3.8% organic, with 1.2% volume, 2.1% pricing, and flat mix. Europe faced headwinds from 8% energy-driven inflation and regulatory pressures like the UK's HFSS advertising restrictions, compressing volumes in impulse categories. However, we gained traction in healthier hydration—our EuroPure alkaline waters surged 14% in Germany and France, capitalizing on the €12B functional water market growing at 9% CAGR per Euromonitor. In the UK, our partnership with Tesco for exclusive low-cal RTD teas drove 2x distribution velocity. We're investing €50M in sustainable sourcing for cocoa to de-risk our chocolate-coated snacks.

Asia-Pacific (15% of revenue): Our growth engine at 9.1% organic, propelled by 4.5% volume and 3.9% pricing, now our fastest-growing region for the third straight quarter. China delivered 12% growth on our premium bubble tea line, partnering for co-branded ready-to-drink formats amid the 15% CAGR in China's $30B RTD tea market. In Southeast Asia, Indonesia and Vietnam saw 18% uplift from affordable hydration packs, leveraging new aseptic filling lines in Jakarta that boosted capacity 30% and reduced waste by 15%. Mix improved via premium adult beverages like sake-infused sparkling waters.

Latin America (5% of revenue): 2.9% organic growth, tempered by 22% hyperinflation in Brazil and Argentina but offset by 4.2% pricing power. Volumes were flat as consumers traded down, but we protected margins through SKU rationalization—eliminating 15% of low-velocity economy packs—and focus on resilient categories like powdered beverages, up 8%. In Mexico, our Aguas Frescas line grew 11%, gaining share in the $5B non-carb segment. We're deploying $20M in precision agriculture tech for sugarcane.

Looking forward, we're confident in sustaining 5-7% organic growth in FY '24, anchored by innovation velocity (10 new SKUs launching Q4), supply chain resilience (AI-driven demand forecasting reduced stockouts 25%), and channel expansion (targeting 20% convenience store penetration gains globally).

Sixth, analyzing organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year: Organic sales growth is our key metric for underlying business performance, excluding acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange. We delivered a strong 5.2% organic sales growth in Q2, driven by 2.8% volume gains, 1.7% pricing actions, and 0.7% favorable mix shift toward our premium health & wellness portfolio. For the first half fiscal 2024, we achieved 4.8% organic growth, ahead of our initial guide.

Looking ahead to Q3 fiscal 2024, we are guiding for organic sales growth of 3% to 5%. This reflects a seasonally softer quarter, lapping last year's strong comps. Volume: Expect 1-2% growth, supported by market share gains in core categories. In snacks, we're seeing 2.5% household penetration uplift from our NutriCrunch high-protein bar line, now 12% of segment sales. Beverages should deliver 1.5% volume, bolstered by the rollout of our zero-sugar VitaQuench functional water, targeting the $15B+ RTD hydration market where we've gained 150 bps share per Nielsen data. Pricing and Mix: 2-3% contribution, with targeted pricing of 1.5-2% to offset 4-6% input cost inflation. Health-focused SKUs like plant-based yogurts and organic ready-to-drink coffees now make up 28% of total sales, delivering 200 bps of margin accretion.

Regionally: North America (65% of sales): 4-6% organic growth, fueled by e-commerce acceleration (now 18% of channel mix) and club channel strength with Costco and Sam's Club. EMEA (20% of sales): 2-4%, with volume recovery in dairy offset by growth in plant-based alternatives amid EU regs. APAC and LatAm (15% of sales): Flat to 2%, cautious due to FX and China’s snacking recovery, but with upside from Brazil's beverage expansion.

For full fiscal 2025, we’re raising our organic sales growth guidance to 4% to 6%, up from prior 3-5%. This is underpinned by a $250M R&D investment yielding 15 new SKUs, including low-cal kombucha extensions and upcycled ingredient snacks to tap the $100B+ global functional foods trend. Supply chain resilience post our cocoa hedging program locks in 70% of 2025 volumes at 15% below spot. Route-to-market optimization via SKU rationalization boosts distribution points by 5% in key chains. We're leaning into 'affordable premium' positioning amid real income erosion.

Risks include commodity volatility, potential U.S. tariff escalations impacting 8% of imports, and shifting preferences toward weight-loss drugs pressuring indulgent categories. But our 42% gross margin gives us pricing power, and we're confident in 50-75 bps of EBITDA margin expansion for FY25. This guidance reflects disciplined execution, outpacing peers through category leadership in health & wellness.

Seventh, examining gross margin analysis drivers and trends: Our gross margin performance continues to be a standout story for the quarter and a testament to our disciplined execution amid volatility. Gross margin is our North Star metric in Food & Beverage—it reflects pricing power, cost discipline, and our ability to navigate commodity headwinds and shifting consumer preferences toward premium products.

For Q2, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 38.7%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points sequentially. This marks our sixth straight quarter of expansion, bringing our trailing 12-month margin to 37.9%, well ahead of our long-term target of 37-39%. This outperforms the industry average of 35-36% as reported by peers.

Margin expansion was driven by strategic pricing actions contributing +320 basis points. We implemented targeted price increases averaging 4.2% across the portfolio, with the heaviest lifts in Snacks—our NutriCrunch plant-based protein bars saw 5-7% hikes justified by clean-label innovation. This was possible due to resilient demand; Nielsen shows our premium snack category grew 8% volume-wise in North America. We limited increases to 2.5% on value-pack beverages to preserve share in club stores.

Offsetting this were input cost pressures, shaving off -110 basis points. Cocoa costs up 25% due to crop shortfalls in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, sugar volatile at +15% from Brazilian disruptions, dairy +3%. Freight added -40 basis points as ocean rates rose 12% amid Red Sea rerouting. We mitigated through forward commodity hedging, locking in 85% of 2024 cocoa at $3,200 per metric ton, and multi-sourcing.

A key tailwind was favorable product mix, adding +140 basis points. Higher-margin Health & Wellness beverages like our zero-sugar electrolyte line grew 15% and carry 45% gross margins. We're pruning lower-margin legacy products; branded premium now 62% of sales.

Regionally, North America margins hit 41.2%, +250 bps YoY, fueled by premiumization in retail channels. Europe saw 37.5% margins, +180 bps, despite HFSS regs; our low-sugar yogurts offset wheat costs. APAC and Latin America faced pressure at 34.8% and 35.2% due to FX and palm oil inflation, but localized sourcing reduced landed costs by 7%.

We've engineered structural uplift through $150 million in Industry 4.0 automation across 12 plants, delivering 2.5% COGS savings this quarter. Sustainable sourcing: 75% of cocoa Rainforest Alliance certified, reducing risk premiums by 5-10%. Inventory optimization trimmed working capital by 15 days.

Strategically, we're positioning for sustained 200+ bps annual expansion via portfolio optimization, exiting 10% of SKUs below 35% margins, 3-5% pricing into 2025, and stabilizing commodity forecasts. Our trajectory underscores innovation-led mix shift, operational excellence, and proactive risk management—we're outrunning inflation.

Eighth, considering impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: One of the most pressing headwinds we've navigated this quarter is the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions. We've seen these pressures acutely, but our proactive strategies have shielded profitability.

Input cost inflation year-to-date was 18% YoY in COGS, driven by agricultural inputs up 22%—wheat +28% from Russia-Ukraine effects and U.S. Plains weather, corn +19% from El Niño, sugar +15% from India/Brazil shortfalls. Non-ag inputs: edible oils +25% amid export curbs, dairy +12% from EU heatwaves, aluminum +14%, PET +11%, ocean freight +30% from Red Sea, natural gas +8% in Europe. This translated to 320 bps of gross margin compression quarter-over-quarter, from 38.2% to 38.7% blended after pricing clawback. EBITDA margins held at 14.8% thanks to $150 million in productivity savings.

Supply chain disruptions amplified this, with lead times up 25% YoY to 56 days due to port congestion at LA/Long Beach, Panama Canal draughts, and trucker shortages. Stockouts hit 12% of SKUs, particularly cocoa products from Ivory Coast harvest drops and EU regs.

Regionally, North America (55% of revenue): Moderate trucking delays, but pricing power passed through 85% of inflation, maintaining 12% beverage volume growth. Europe (25%): Energy inflation +16%, Rhine disruptions hit grains, UK lines at 85% capacity. APAC (15%): Monsoons slashed rice yields 14%, China port delays. LatAm (5%): Sugar normalized.

Strategically, our AI-powered supply chain platform on SAP IBP improved forecasting to 92%, reducing excess inventory 18%. Hedging covers 70% of 2024 wheat/corn at 10-15% below futures. Supplier diversification shifted 25% palm oil sourcing. Vertical integration: $300 million in U.S. corn processing internalizes 15% HFCS needs.

Product actions: Rationalized 8% low-margin SKUs, premium beverages grew 22% volumes. Regenerative Ag sequesters 50,000 tons CO2e, securing wheat at 5% discounts.

Forward, input inflation moderates to 8-10% YoY, disruptions persist but onshoring trims lead times 20%. We've baked in $400 million pricing tailwinds, targeting 37.5% gross margin and 10-12% EBITDA growth. Our 65% inflation pass-through outperforms peers, positioning for share gains.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
